newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HSBC's Purves positive on 1997.
newsitem.headline: HSBC's Purves positive on 1997.

text.p: Banking group HSBC Holdings Plc's key Hong Kong operations remain the largest component of profits but the contribution is shrinking as the bank's overseas expansion pays off, group chairman William Purves said on Monday.
"We may be the most profitable bank of our size in the world," Purves told a news conference in Hong Kong.

The percentage contribution of Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corp, the key entity of the HSBC Holdings Plc group, has declined, especially since the bank's acquisition of Midland Bank Plc in 1992 but it continues to be the single largest contributor to earnings, said Purves.
The Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corp reported an attributable profit of HK$19.25 billion, an increase of 16 percent over 1995.
Its 61.5 percent owned subsidiary, Hang Seng Bank Ltd, reported a net profit of HK$8.49 billion, up six percent over 1995.

"Despite intense competition in all of our markets, our net interest margins improved, although as expected, there was some contraction in Hong Kong in the second half of the year. Costs were well contained," said Purves.
"These results suggest that we are in pretty good shape for whatever happens," Purves said when asked how the bank was preparing itself for the handover to Chinese rule.
The British territory will be handed back to China on June 30, 1997 after more than 150 years of British rule.
"We will continue to invest in Hong Kong and China," said Purves.
"We are taking a positive view rather than a negative view than you see so often in the press," he said.
"We will continue to adjust our business as political and economic conditions suggest we need to," he said without elaborating.
He said the diversification overseas was the culmination of a strategy launched in 1981 to develop from a regional into a global organisation.
HSBC Holdings Plc reported a 1996 pre-tax profit of 4.52 billion sterling against 3.67 billion in 1995.
